title: allow(dead_code)/allow(unreachable_code) used where #[cfg(target_os)] belongs
description:
persona/src/main.rs uses lint suppressions to work around platform-conditional code that `#[cfg]` expresses directly.

Site 1, line 8-9:
    #[allow(dead_code)] // used only on macOS via #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
    const LAUNCHD_PLIST: &str = "...";

The comment states the intent exactly, and `#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]` is the attribute that means it. As written, the 1.2 KiB plist string is compiled into every Linux and Windows `persona` binary, and the `allow` suppresses dead-code detection permanently — if the macOS branch is ever deleted or renamed, nothing will report that the constant is now unreferenced on all platforms.

Site 2, lines 495-517, `install_service()`:
    #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
    { ...; return Ok(()); }
    #[allow(unreachable_code)]
    { // Linux / systemd path ... }

The systemd branch is guarded by `#[allow(unreachable_code)]` rather than `#[cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))]`. On macOS the whole systemd block is still type-checked and codegen'd behind an early `return`, and the `allow` blanket-suppresses unreachable-code warnings for the entire block — including any genuinely unreachable statement introduced later inside it.

Fix: `#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]` on the constant, and split `install_service` into two `#[cfg]`-gated bodies (or two functions) so neither `allow` is needed. Both suppressions then disappear.
close_reason: Duplicate of persona-5s4b.26 (filed first, equivalent detail).
